title: Small Hours — conversations with people who make things by hand
description: A fortnightly podcast recorded in workshops, kitchens and sheds: an hour with someone who makes things by hand, and how they learned to.

sections.title: An hour in someone else's workshop.
sections.lede: Potters, luthiers, bookbinders, a woman who repairs church clocks. Recorded where they work, with the tools still running.

sections.title: Episodes
sections.body: Every episode has its full transcript, and chapters you can jump between.

episodes.title: 14. The clock in the tower, with Ruth Okonkwo
episodes.summary: Ruth has kept the same church clock running for twenty-two years. We climb the tower with her on a winding day.

transcript.text: We are about ninety steps up, and Ruth has not stopped talking once.
Forty turns for the time, forty for the strike. You count them, or you lose your place.

episodes.title: 13. Glaze that remembers the kiln, with Tomas Lind
episodes.summary: A potter who mixes every glaze from the ash of the wood that fires it.

transcript.text: Apple wood gives you a green you cannot buy. Oak gives you a brown that looks like weather.

sections.title: The reel
sections.body: Ninety seconds from this season's workshops, with captions.

media.alt: Hands at work: a potter's wheel, a lathe, a clock's escapement, a bookbinder's needle

sections.text: I listen while I work. It is the only podcast that sounds like my own workshop.
